segments.text: Travelling from Parthasarathy Temple to Marina Beach

segments.name: Marina Beach
segments.description: Marina beach in Chennai along the Bay of Bengal is India's longest and world's second longest beach. This predominantly sandy of nearly 12 kilometers extends from Beasant Nagar in the south to Fort St. George in the north. Chennai Marina beach was renovated by Governor Mountstuart Elphinstone Grant Duff in 1880s.

Built in neo-Gothic style, the church delights every visitor with its naturally lit interiors, rows of wooden pews and striking windows with coloured panes.

segments.text: Travelling from Santhome Cathedral Basilica to Vadapalani Murugan Temple

segments.name: Vadapalani Murugan Temple
segments.description: The Arulmigu Vadapalani Murugan Temple is a famous Hindu temple in Chennai, dedicated to Lord Murugan. It was founded in the late 19th century from a humble thatched hut and is now a grand temple known for its divine power, architectural details like the Rajagopuram with Skanda Purana scenes, and a unique idol of Lord Murugan wearing footwear, symbolizing his eagerness to help devotees. The temple complex includes numerous shrines to other deities, a temple tank, and large halls for events.

segments.name: Vivekanandar House
segments.description: Vivekananda House or Vivekanandar Illam in Chennai played a significant part in the spread of Ramakrishna Movement in South India. Swami Vivekananda stayed here for nine days in 1897, after his return from the West. Sri Ramakrishna Math's Chennai unit functioned here from 1897 to 1906.

segments.description: The museum has mainly six buildings. The main building has a fine archaeological section representing all the major South Indian periods, including Chola, Vijayanagara, Hoysala and Chalukya. It also has a fine ethnology collection. The front building has a collection of arms, puppets and other art pieces.
